subject: Using predict and predictDsurface to obtain a density estimate from a fitted model with a continuous habitat covariate

messages.author: 893322b7081eeb7e
messages.subject: Using predict and predictDsurface to obtain a density estimate from a fitted model with a continuous habitat covariate
parts:
Hello,

I am on the final steps of an analysis and have fitted a model with a continuous habitat covariate (proportion dense understory) for a mutlisession model where sites were surveyed on 2 occasions in 2018 and 2 occasions in 2019. There are 2 objectives I'm trying to achieve: 1) obtain a single density estimate for the population within the mask area from the fitted model with the continuous habitat covariate; 2) predict the density into a larger landscape using a new mask that includes sites that have habitat covariate data, but were not surveyed for abundance of the study species.

I have tried predict() and predictDsurface(). The output gives me density estimates for each unique value of my covariate (proportion dense understory), making me think it is being treated as categorical rather than continuous. In addition, I think I have an error in my approach with predictDsurface() because I am not seeing results in plot(). Apologies for posing another question to the group, but I was unable to troubleshoot this with the manual or by searching through previous discussion topics in this group.

Many thanks in advance for any suggestions, my code and output are below and my input files are attached.

Best,
Melissa


captures1819<- read.table("londonCapt.txt")

#create trapfile
trapfile18<- read.traps("london_proxtrap_18.txt", detector = "proximity")
trapfile19<- read.traps("london_proxtrap_19.txt", detector = "proximity")
trapfile<-list(trapfile18,trapfile19)

#2018mask
mask1<- read.mask(file = "londonMask18.txt", spacing = 30)
covariates18 <- read.mask('londonMask18_covariates.txt')
mask1<- addCovariates(mask1,covariates18, strict=FALSE, replace=FALSE)

covariates(mask1)
head(mask1)

maskarea(mask1)

#2019mask
mask2<- read.mask(file = "londonMask19.txt", spacing = 30)
covariates19 <- read.mask('londonMask19_covariates.txt')
mask2<- addCovariates(mask2,covariates19, strict=FALSE, replace=FALSE)

covariates(mask2)
maskarea(mask2)


#metapop1819mask
mask <-list(mask1,mask2)
covariates(mask)


#make.capthist:
CHmetapop <-make.capthist(captures1819, trapfile, 
                          fmt = "XY", noccasions = 2, tol = 3, snapXY = TRUE)

summary(CHmetapop, terse=TRUE)
verify(CHmetapop, report = 2)


V3PropDensU.fit <- secr.fit (CHmetapop, model = list(D~V3, g0~session, sigma~session), CL = FALSE, detectfn = 0, 
                             method = "Newton-Raphson", mask=mask)


# Looking to obtain a single density estimate for the population in the fitted surface from V3PropDenseU.fit, but I get a density estimate for each value of the covariate (it should be a continuous covariate (proportion dense understory), but maybe it is being treated as categorical?)
covariateD <- predict(V3PropDensU.fit, save=TRUE)
covariateD

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Using predict and predictDsurface to obtain a density estimate from a fitted model with a continuous habitat covariate
parts:
It does seem that secr.make.newdata() was ignoring all.levels = FALSE in this configuration (a bug now fixed for the next version). However, it is definitely treating V3 as numeric, not factor.

You can always specify newdata directly:
predict(V3PropDensU.fit, newdata = data.frame(session = 1:2, V3 = 0.605), save=TRUE)

The output from predictDsurface is a Dsurface object, a special sort of mask with its own plot method. Check ?predictDsurface and its examples.
surfaces <- predictDsurface(V3PropDensU.fit)
par(mfrow = c(2,1))
plot(surfaces)

mean(covariates(surfaces[[1]])$D.0)  # average predicted density over mask 1

I'm surprised  by the small number of points on each mask. These animals are absolutely restricted to small habitat patches?

Best,
Melissa
